determinismProtocol.environmentRule: Platform (OS and RID) is a determinism dimension (contract rules.platformDeterminism). Every supported RID in eng/z3-consumers.json is a registered environment. compiler-verifier runs on linux-x64 only, the only platform its release gates use; the protocol establishes nothing for it on another platform and says so in every result. Runner labels are pinned (no -latest label). The runner image version cannot be pinned on hosted runners; every attempt records ImageOS and ImageVersion, and a disagreement is never excused by an image change.

checkout.rule: Every environment checks out the committed bytes (git config --global core.autocrlf false before checkout). Inputs are byte-identical on every platform, so any platform difference comes from the code under test. This is an input pin, not a normalization: no output is ever converted. Tracked files must be unmodified before the first attempt and after every invocation (git status --porcelain --untracked-files=no is empty); otherwise that invocation and every later attempt in the job are invalid.

releaseEpoch.rule: Amendment 1.7.0 (maintainer decision D-G2-RAISE-CAP-2-RUNS, 2026-10-20, 'Raise cap to 2,100, 2 runs'): the epoch's first execution (run 7, v025-reproof-1, on 48cae911, 397 runner-minutes) came back INCOMPLETE because osx-arm64 job 2 hit its 50-minute timeout (harness cut at 45). The 0.25 epoch (every run after run 6, epochAfterRunNumber) now has a ceiling of 2,100 runner-minutes (epochCeilingRunnerMinutes; 1,600 before). Its remaining executions form a window of every run after run 7 (afterRunNumber): at most 2 executions (maxExecutions), on the commit the candidate manifest names (the 1.6.0 binding), which may be executed twice (maxExecutionsPerCandidate). In the window every osx-arm64 execution job has a 70-minute timeout (jobTimeoutMinutes); every other timeout is unchanged, and the registered environment table and the 0.24 budget stay as they were. One window execution's worst case is 5 + 10 + 2 x (70 + 50 + 70 + 110 + 110) = 835 (worstCasePerExecution), so the window's is 2 x 835 = 1,670 (worstCaseWithEpochTimeouts) and the epoch's 397 + 1,670 = 2,067 <= 2,100. The window may spend 2,100 - 397 = 1,703 (ceilingRunnerMinutes). worstCaseTotal keeps the 1.6.0 formula over the registered environment table (2 x 795 = 1,590), which the earlier validator also checks; the binding worst case is worstCaseWithEpochTimeouts. The plan step charges every epoch run to the 2,100 ceiling and reserves the 835 worst case for this run. For the candidate commit only, the one-execution-per-commit rule and the non-docs-change-after-a-failed-execution rule are replaced by the limit of 2. The second execution of the candidate runs only after the first was decided INCOMPLETE with no DISAGREE and no AGREE-FAIL, and that decided record is committed on protected main at priorResultPath (with {runId} the first execution's run id), which the plan step reads; a NON-DETERMINISTIC or FAILING first execution, or one without its record, ends the epoch for the candidate. Both executions are retained and reported. Everything else is unchanged: no attempt, job or run is re-run, no control run, and the same cases, environments, attempts, agreement rate, decider and record format.

amendment160.rule: Amendment 1.6.0 (maintainer decision D-G2-TWO-RUNS, 2026-10-19, 'Amend: 2 runs for 0.25'): every run of the protocol workflow numbered after run 6 (c2-1424-regen-3, the last 0.24 execution) belongs to the 0.25 epoch. The epoch allows at most 2 executions and no dispatched control run, and charges only its own runs to its own ceiling of 1,600 runner-minutes; under the protocol's worst-case formula 2 x 795 = 1,590. An execution runs only on the commit that candidate.commit of the 0.25 candidate manifest (candidateManifest, read from protected main by the plan step) names; a missing, unreadable or different manifest refuses. The candidate SHA is not known before the freeze, so the binding is to the manifest, not to a literal SHA. If the candidate is re-frozen, the manifest names the new commit. Everything else in the frozen rule is unchanged: one execution per commit, a non-docs change after a failed execution, no retry or re-run, and the same cases, environments, attempts, agreement rate, decider and record format. The 1.5.0 extraExecution binding applies only to the 0.24 runs.
